title: Git facts off the request path
summary: Decision-ready architecture for Git facts in Agent Studio. Inventories the ten request paths that still spawn Git or walk history at 9e2526be5. The card list is Git-free; the card is not, because every switch loads provenance, commit files with the default diff, and a result history that walks all refs. Recommends a generation-keyed SQLite fact store with one writer per repository: interim on the backend, target tables in task-server.db fed by a fenced runner-host producer. Invalidation is by ref fingerprint and configuration generation, never by task event. Restored generations make a restart serve without Git, and transactional publish with a producer epoch covers crashes. Eight bounded slices, guardrails first, target card list and card detail under 200 ms with zero Git processes per read. D1 to D8 carry working recommendations; AGT-2954 is found integrated and AGT-3041 fixed.

implementationTasks.title: S1 Guard Git spawns on read requests and enforce budgets as tests
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S1 Guard Git spawns on read requests and enforce budgets as tests

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, sections 01 (request paths R1 to R10), 03 (fault isolation, budgets) and 04 (S1); decisions D6 and D7. This slice lands first so later slices cannot regress.

## Change

1. Route every Git process start through one boundary. Today `GitService.RunGitProcess` (`backend/Features/Git/GitService.cs:8259`) is bypassed by `TaskFileHistoryService.RunGit` (`backend/Features/Tasks/TaskFileHistoryService.cs:585-604`), `GitService.RollbackGitArgs` (`:6661`), `RemoteReviewPlanBuilder.Git` (`backend/Features/Runner/RemoteReviewPlanBuilder.cs:399-422`), `CommitCandidateGate.cs:628`, `PublishActionService.cs:338-392` and `WorkspaceArtifactPushWorker.cs:211`. Move them onto a shared `GitProcess` runner that records `GitProcessTelemetry` and registers children.
2. Add an ambient read-request scope, set by endpoint metadata on every GET route and on the board read gate. At the boundary, a Git start inside that scope throws `GitProcessOnReadRequestException` in Debug and test builds. In production it counts, logs the route and command, and raises a health warning (D6). Write routes and background services are not affected.
3. Open telemetry scopes on the routes that have none: `/commits*`, `/commit*`, `/runs/*`, `/result-history*`.
4. Add an allowlist of the known violating read routes (R4 to R8 in the Dossier) as a checked-in list. A test fails when a route outside the list spawns, and when the list grows. Each later slice removes its entries.
5. Add a load fixture: 3,000 cards, at least 2,000 archived, 200 or more in review, two cards with the same id, a repository with packed refs and a worktree.

## Budget tests

- `GET /api/tasks/` and `/grouped`: 0 Git spawns; serialized size per card at most 2 KiB on the fixture.
- `/core` and `/details/*`: 0 Git spawns.
- One `GitStateIndexService` run on the fixture with unchanged refs completes and its spawn count is recorded as the baseline for S2.
- Record a 30-switch baseline per route (p50, p95, spawns) with `TaskOperationTimingFilter` and keep it in the card results.

Do not change caching or the producer in this slice.

acceptanceScope.slice: S1 Guard Git spawns on read requests and enforce budgets as tests
criteria: Every Git process start in backend/ goes through one boundary that records telemetry.
A Git spawn inside a read request throws in tests and Debug, and is counted and warned in production.
Budget tests assert 0 spawns for list, grouped, core and details on a 3,000-card fixture with duplicate ids.
The violator allowlist exists, contains only R4 to R8 routes, and a test fails if it grows.
A 30-switch baseline per route with p50, p95 and spawn counts is recorded in the card results.

implementationTasks.title: S2 Persist Git fact generations and restore them on start
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S2 Persist Git fact generations and restore them on start

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 03 (the fact store, writers, invalidation, cold start and crash recovery) and section 04 (S2); decisions D1, D3 and D7. Depends on S1.

## Change

1. Add the Git fact store as SQLite `git-facts.db` in the backend state directory with the tables `git_repositories`, `git_ref_generations`, `card_git_facts` and `fact_producer_health`, exactly as the Dossier specifies. Keep the schema in one place so S7 can create the same tables in `task-server/TaskServerStore.cs`.
2. Make `GitStateIndexService` the only writer. Publish each repository generation (ref object IDs, ref fingerprint, `config_generation`, settings version, producer epoch, card rows) in one transaction in WAL mode, then swap the in-memory pointer that `TaskListGitProjectionCache` reads. Reject a publish whose producer epoch is lower than the stored one.
3. On start, load the last generation per repository and serve it with state `restored` and its age. Compute `ReadOnlyGitRefFingerprint` and the configuration signature from files. If both match, mark it `ready` without starting Git. Otherwise run a normal delta run.
4. Advance `config_generation` only from the existing watcher events for `config`, `config.worktree` and included files (`GitStateIndexService.cs:309-325`). Do not spawn `git config --list` at the start of every run (`:477`). A task event must not start Git when no card's input signature changed.
5. Run `PRAGMA quick_check` on open. On failure, move the file aside, raise a typed health event and rebuild within the spawn budget, answering `warming` per card.
6. Replace the repository-wide abort after `min(3, n)` card failures (`TaskListGitProjectionCache.cs:392-393`) with a repository health state that keeps the last good generation.

Do not change what is computed per card in this slice; S3 does that.

acceptanceScope.slice: S2 Persist Git fact generations and restore them on start
criteria: Restart with unchanged refs serves restored Git facts before any Git process and reaches ready with 0 spawns.
A task event that changes no card input signature starts 0 Git processes.
Killing the process during a run leaves the previous generation current and readable.
A publish with an older producer epoch is rejected in a test.
A corrupt store file is detected on start and rebuilt without request-time Git.

implementationTasks.title: S3 Serve card Git facts and the default diff from the store
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S3 Serve card Git facts and the default diff from the store

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 03 (invalidation by ref generation, reads) and section 04 (S3). Depends on S2. Diff object keys follow `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html` D1.

## Change

1. Add `git_commit_facts` (parents, tree, author time, subject, trailers, name-status and numstat per path), keyed by repository and SHA, immutable. The producer fills it for new SHAs in one batched read per run, for example `git log --no-walk --name-status --numstat` or `cat-file --batch`.
2. Add `git_reachability` per target ref. On a fast-forward from `old` to `new`, append `rev-list old..new`. On a non-fast-forward move, recompute that ref once. Classify all cards by an in-memory join. Enable `core.commitGraph` and `fetch.writeCommitGraph` on managed checkouts.
3. Take a card's attributed SHAs from `task.json` and `result_handoffs` as its input signature. Stop `log --all --grep` (`GitService.cs:6965`) on read paths, and move the attribution backfill out of the `/commits` GET (`TaskGitEndpoints.cs:418`) into the producer.
4. Serve these from the store with generation, age and ETag, and with 0 Git spawns:
   - `/provenance` (replaces the per-commit `merge-base` calls in `TaskProvenanceService.cs:358-366`)
   - `/commits`, `/commits/files` and `/commit`
   - `/commits/{sha}/files`
   - `/runs/{i}/commits` and `/runs/{i}/files`
5. At publication, the producer writes a SHA-keyed diff object for each attributed commit and for the aggregate. The default diff that `git-pane.service.ts:331-343` selects is served from that object. A missing object answers `warming` and queues a priority computation.
6. Remove these routes from the S1 allowlist.

acceptanceScope.slice: S3 Serve card Git facts and the default diff from the store
criteria: Provenance, commits, commits/files, commit and the default diff spawn 0 Git processes on the request thread.
Each of those routes has p95 under 200 ms on the 3,000-card fixture over a 30-switch replay.
A single fast-forward of the target ref is reflected in all card facts within 2 s on the fixture.
A non-fast-forward move removes containment and is covered by a test.
The S1 allowlist no longer contains R4, R5 or the run file routes.

implementationTasks.title: S4 Serve result history from a version index
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S4 Serve result history from a version index

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 01 (R6), section 03 (writers) and section 04 (S4); decision D4. Depends on S1 only.

## Change

1. Add `result_versions` (task key, version id, producer, lane, run index, verdict, steps, timestamp, content hash, source commit) to the Git fact store.
2. Make `ResultVersionStore` (`backend/Features/Tasks/Results/ResultVersionStore.cs`) the writer: each time it snapshots a prior `status.md` into `results/history/`, it also writes the index row. Content stays in the task folder snapshot.
3. Add a one-time background backfill that imports legacy versions from workspace history, using the logic of `TaskFileHistoryService.GetWorkspaceResultHistory` (`TaskFileHistoryService.cs:141-218`). It runs per project within the spawn budget, can resume, and records progress in `fact_producer_health`.
4. Make `ResultHistoryQueryService.List` and `Read` (`ResultHistoryQueryService.cs:29`, `:86`) read only the index and the snapshot files. For a version that is not yet imported, answer it as `warming`, without walking history. Remove the double walk in `Read`.
5. Remove `/result-history` from the S1 allowlist.

acceptanceScope.slice: S4 Serve result history from a version index
criteria: GET result-history and result-history/{versionId} spawn 0 Git processes.
result-history p95 is under 50 ms and does not grow with the number of versions on the fixture.
Backfill is resumable, budgeted and reports progress; a not-yet-imported version answers warming.
New status.md versions appear in the index at write time without a Git read.

implementationTasks.title: S5 Remove request-time scans from the board and persist the slim board
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S5 Remove request-time scans from the board and persist the slim board

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 01 (R1, R3), section 03 (cold start) and section 04 (S5). Depends on S1. Coordinate with `docs/task-switch-performance/index.html` card 5 ("Reuse board records across task navigation").

## Change

1. In `TaskIndexCache.EnsureFresh` (`backend/Features/Tasks/TaskIndexCache.cs:408-480`), stop letting a request become the refresher (`:446-451`). A request reads the current snapshot and signals the background refresher. Mutation paths that need read-your-write keep the existing published-generation wait, bounded at 2 s.
2. Persist the last published slim board summaries (`BoardCardSummary`) per project, with their index generation. On start, serve them as `restored` while the first background scan runs, instead of blocking on it (`:454-457`).
3. Remove the `ScanAllJobs` call from the legacy detail route (`TaskCrudEndpoints.cs:404`); use the reference index snapshot.
4. Keep the AGT-2703 ETag contract and the single-flight memo in `BoardReadConcurrencyGate`; add the persisted generation to the signature.

acceptanceScope.slice: S5 Remove request-time scans from the board and persist the slim board
criteria: No board, core or detail request runs TaskIndexCache.Refresh on its own thread; a test asserts it.
GET /api/tasks/ and /grouped have p95 under 200 ms at the current board size and on the 3,000-card fixture.
The first board read after process start answers within 2 s from the persisted board, marked restored.
ETag and 304 behaviour is unchanged for unchanged inputs.

implementationTasks.title: S6 Take Git out of mutation handlers and review replanning
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S6 Take Git out of mutation handlers and review replanning

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 01 (R9, R10), section 03 (mutations and review planning) and section 04 (S6); decision D5. Depends on S2.

## Change

1. Add a producer request: "publish a generation at least as new as ref fingerprint X". The producer deduplicates requests and serves them ahead of sweeps.
2. Replace direct `TaskIntegrationStatusService.BuildLookup` calls on request threads with that request plus a store read, bounded at 2 s:
   - `TaskTransitionService.cs:316` inside `MoveAsync`, and the other transition call sites at `:1688`, `:1707`, `:1740` and `:1816`
   - `TaskIntegrationRecoveryEndpoints.cs:40`
   If the bound is reached, return 409 `integration-check-pending` with a retry hint. The Studio retries once and shows the pending state.
3. Queue project-settings-triggered replanning (`ProjectSettingsEndpoints.cs:1415-1442`) to `ReviewInfrastructureRetryScheduler` instead of running per attempt inside the request.
4. Keep the authoritative acceptance checks exactly as strict as today. A display cache never bypasses them; the check reads a generation proven current for the ref fingerprint.

acceptanceScope.slice: S6 Take Git out of mutation handlers and review replanning
criteria: A completion move and a project settings write start 0 Git processes on the request thread.
Completion move p95 stays under 2.2 s including the producer wait; timeouts return a typed 409.
Queued review attempts are replanned in the background with the same plans as before, proven by a test.
Acceptance outcomes on the existing acceptance test suite are unchanged.

implementationTasks.title: S7 Publish Git fact generations from the runner host
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S7 Publish Git fact generations from the runner host

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, sections 02 (option C), 03 (writers, epoch) and 04 (S7); decision D1. Depends on S3 and on AGT-2737 B6 readiness. Extends, and does not repeat, the cards "Git object contract and Task Server store" and "Runner publication of Git facts and diff objects" in `docs/studio-route-ownership/index.html`, which own diff objects.

## Change

1. Create the S2 and S3 tables in `task-server/TaskServerStore.cs` with the same schema, inside `InWriteTransactionAsync`, and include them in `FullBackupService`.
2. On the runner host, beside the canonical checkout (ADR-0073), run one fact producer per repository under a Task Server lease with a monotonic epoch. Publish generations as a new outbox kind `runner.git-generation`. The payload carries repository id, ref object IDs, config generation, new commit facts, reachability delta, card rows, epoch and checksum, and its ingestion is idempotent. Give the existing `runner.git-facts` event (`runner/DurableHandoffPayloads.cs:28-34`) a reader, or fold it in.
3. The Task Server validates epoch and monotonic generation and stores atomically. Readers in the Studio go through the Task Server projection.
4. Run in shadow for one repository: both producers publish, and a comparer reports mismatched card facts. Then cut over per repository, and stop the backend producer for that repository.

acceptanceScope.slice: S7 Publish Git fact generations from the runner host
criteria: Task Server ingestion rejects an older epoch and a non-monotonic generation in tests.
One week of shadow run reports zero mismatched card facts for the pilot repository.
After cutover, the task server host starts 0 Git processes for facts of that repository.
Board and card reads keep their S3 to S5 budgets through the Task Server.

implementationTasks.title: S8 Benchmark Git readers and repository maintenance
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# S8 Benchmark Git readers and repository maintenance

Source: `docs/git-facts-architecture/index.html`, section 02 (option D) and section 04 (S8); decision D8. Depends on S3.

## Change

Benchmark these readers for the producer's operations: resolve refs, merge-base and reachability delta, name-status and numstat for a SHA, effective config, and a single file patch.

- the bounded CLI
- one long-lived `git cat-file --batch` and `--batch-check` reader
- LibGit2Sharp
- a small gitoxide sidecar

Use identical fixtures on Windows and Linux: packed refs, worktrees, conditional includes, shallow history, missing objects, concurrent ref movement and the 3,000-card fixture. Measure cold and warm, process start, total CPU, memory, p50 and p95, and correctness against CLI output. Measure the effect of these maintenance settings on the same fixture:

- `core.commitGraph`
- `fetch.writeCommitGraph`
- scheduled `git maintenance`
- `core.fsmonitor` with `core.untrackedCache`, only where status is still needed

Record the decision in the Dossier implementation log. Adopt a library only with a CPU reduction of 30 percent or more and full parity.

acceptanceScope.slice: S8 Benchmark Git readers and repository maintenance
criteria: A benchmark report with p50, p95, CPU and correctness per reader and operation on Windows and Linux is in the card results.
Maintenance settings are measured on the same fixture and the chosen settings are applied to managed checkouts.
The adoption decision is recorded with the 30 percent CPU and parity rule applied.
